For large policy counterfactuals such as optimal visitor or commercial taxes, `urbanwelfare` includes a C++-accelerated nonlinear Quantitative Spatial Model (`solve_qsm()`) and an analytical-adjoint Ramsey tax optimizer (`optimal_spatial_tax()`) calibrated directly to the validated `urban_account` and estimated sector price shares $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\kappa}}^S$.

```{r}
library(urbanwelfare)

sim <- sim_urban_city(N = 40, T = 8, tourism_share = 0.14, seed = 202)
acct <- urban_account(sim$E_R0, sim$H_0, sim$origins, sim$destinations)
exps <- build_exposures(acct, sim$shocks)
fit  <- estimate_bilateral(sim$bilateral_panel, exps)
welf <- recover_welfare(fit, acct, se_method = "none")

# Solve both empirical first-order Ramsey taxes and nonlinear QSM adjoint optimum
tax <- optimal_spatial_tax(
  welfare = welf,
  account = acct,
  demand_elasticities = list(sigma_T = 7.0, eta_out = 2.5),
  mode = "both"
)
summary(tax)

plot(tax, type = "distribution")
```
